name: code-shell
description: Coding loop: read, edit, patch, run tests, format and analyze code.

commands.name: fix
commands.description: Reproduce and fix a defect in the workspace
commands.template: Reproduce and fix the following defect in the workspace, then run the tests: {input}

commands.name: test
commands.description: Write or run the failing test first
commands.template: Write or run the failing test for: {input}. Show the failing command and output first, then the smallest fix, then the passing run.

commands.name: review
commands.description: Review a change for concrete risks
commands.template: Review the change described by: {input}. Report correctness, security and regression risks with file:line evidence; no style-only findings.

tools.name: run_shell
tools.description: Executes a terminal command. Only whitelisted commands are allowed (ls, find, grep, git, echo, cat, head, tail, wc, mkdir, cp, mv, python, node, npm, ...); destructive patterns (rm, sudo, > /dev/, ...) are blocked. The user sees a confirmation prompt before execution and can deny it — on denial you receive a message that the command was not approved; then choose a different path.

command.description: The terminal command, e.g. 'git status' or 'npm install'

cwd.description: Optional working directory inside the active workspace, e.g. 'src' or 'tests' (workspace-relative, not an absolute path).

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Reads the contents of a file and returns its text with 1-based line numbers (N-tab format). Supports plain text, code, Markdown, and PDF files. Optional offset (1-based start line) and limit (line count, default 2000) window the output. Use this tool when the user wants to read, analyze, summarize, or explain a file. For PDF files the text is automatically extracted page by page. Security: Only files in the home directory, Desktop, Documents, Downloads are allowed.

offset.description: 1-based line number to start reading from (for large files).

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Creates or overwrites a file inside the workspace (approval-gated). Use for new files or full rewrites; prefer edit_file for targeted changes.

path.description: Target file path — absolute or ~-relative preferred; a workspace-relative path resolves against the active workspace.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replaces an exact snippet (old_string) in a text file with new_string. Fails safely if old_string is missing or ambiguous — no partial writes; set replace_all=true to replace every occurrence. Returns a unified diff of the change. Security: Only files in the home directory, Desktop, Documents, Downloads are allowed.

path.description: Absolute or ~-relative path to the text file.

old_string.description: Exact text to replace (must occur exactly once without replace_all; include surrounding context).

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match (default false).

tools.name: run_tests
tools.description: Runs a test command in the workspace (pytest / vitest / npm test / python -m pytest) and returns the output tail. Use this to VERIFY every code change.

cwd.description: Optional working directory inside the active workspace, e.g. 'src' or 'tests' (workspace-relative, not an absolute path).

tools.name: run_linter
tools.description: Runs ruff check (static analysis) over a file or a directory. fix=True applies the automatic corrections.

path.description: Absolute or ~-relative path to the file or directory.

tools.name: format_code
tools.description: Formats a Python file with ruff format (Black-compatible). check_only=True inspects without writing.

path.description: Absolute or ~-relative path to the Python file (.py).

check_only.description: True = inspect only, do not write.

tools.name: scaffold_project
tools.description: Project Factory: creates a complete, runnable project skeleton in one call — manifest, sources, real tests, docs, license, gitignore — then verifies it structurally. Returns PROJECT_SCAFFOLD_VERIFIED only when the verification gate passed. Refuses non-empty target directories (nothing is ever overwritten).

target_dir.description: Absolute or ~-relative path to a fresh directory inside an allowed root (e.g. ~/Projekte/meine-app) that is empty or absent.

template.description: One of: python-cli (default), python-api, node-cli, web-app, generic

author.description: Author name used in the license

tools.name: analyze_project
tools.description: Analyses a local project folder top-down: stack, marker files, test command, risks and next steps. Use this for as-is analyses, codebase reviews and when the user wants to understand or improve an existing project.

path.description: Absolute or ~-relative path to the project folder.

tools.name: file_search
tools.description: Searches the computer for files (macOS: Spotlight, Linux: find). Use this tool when the user is looking for a file on their computer.

query.description: File name or search term, e.g. 'invoice 2026' or 'resume.pdf'

path.description: Optional search root — absolute or ~-relative, e.g. '~/Desktop'. Defaults to the active workspace.

tools.name: load_workspace
tools.description: Reads all files of a directory (workspace) recursively. Use this tool when the user wants to analyse, understand or review a whole project. Ideal for code reviews, project overviews and documentation tasks.

path.description: Path to the directory — absolute or ~-relative, e.g. '~/Desktop/my-project'.

extensions.description: Only load these file extensions, e.g. ['.py', '.md']. Empty = all.

tools.name: list_directory
tools.description: Lists the contents of a directory. Use this tool when the user wants to know what is inside a folder.

path.description: Path to the directory — absolute or ~-relative, e.g. '~/Desktop' or '~/Documents'.
